headline: PAGASA Expands Red Rainfall Warning Across Central Luzon as LPA 08i Stays Inside PAR
seoTitle: Central Luzon Red Rain Warning, LPA 08i Update | FMB News
seoDescription: PAGASA placed Zambales, Pampanga, Bataan and parts of Tarlac and Bulacan under a Red rainfall warning at 5 p.m. on August 28.
deck: Serious flooding was expected in Zambales, Pampanga, Bataan and specified areas of Tarlac and Bulacan as the Habagat persisted and LPA 08i remained east-northeast of Itbayat.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: PAGASA placed Zambales, Pampanga, Bataan and specified areas of Tarlac and Bulacan under a Red rainfall warning at 5 p.m. Friday, August 28, because of the Southwest Monsoon or Habagat.

The weather bureau said serious flooding was expected in flood-prone areas covered by the Red warning. Metro Manila, Rizal and specified areas of Tarlac, Nueva Ecija, Bulacan, Cavite and Batangas were under Orange, where flooding was threatening.

sections.heading: LPA 08i status
paragraphs: At 3 p.m., PAGASA estimated LPA 08i at 560 kilometers east-northeast of Itbayat, Batanes, inside the Philippine Area of Responsibility. The disturbance retained a medium chance of developing into a tropical depression.

Its future development and track remained uncertain. The heavy rain affecting western and central Luzon was tied to the Habagat, which can remain hazardous whether or not the LPA becomes a named cyclone.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: PAGASA's broader heavy-rainfall outlook forecast 100 to 200 millimeters over La Union, Benguet, Bataan, Zambales and Occidental Mindoro during August 28. A rainfall outlook covers a longer period and should not be confused with the shorter-fuse regional warning colors.

Local governments separately announced class suspensions for affected communities, but coverage and learning arrangements varied by locality. Residents should rely on the latest LGU and school advisories rather than assume a province-wide suspension.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Repeated rain can quickly worsen flooding and slope instability. Communities near rivers, drainage channels and steep terrain should follow evacuation, road-closure and safety instructions from local disaster authorities.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: PAGASA scheduled the next rainfall-warning update for 8 p.m. Warning levels and covered municipalities can change within hours, so residents should rely on the latest regional warning, river-basin advisory and local disaster-office instruction.
